title: Copilot Studio topic: leave request with date validation and approval flow
summary: Topic YAML that asks for leave type, dates and a note, validates the date range, calculates the days and hands the request to a Power Automate approval flow.
body:
Topic for the Copilot Studio code editor. The agent collects a leave request in four questions, rejects an end date before the start date, computes the number of calendar days with Power Fx, asks for confirmation and then calls a cloud flow that starts the approval. Replace the flowId with the ID of your own flow that uses the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger and returns an output named requestid.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Collects a leave request (type, start date, end date, reason), validates the dates and submits it to an approval flow.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Request leave
    triggerQueries:
      - I want to request leave
      - Book vacation
      - Submit a holiday request
      - I need time off
      - Apply for annual leave

  actions:
    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_intro
      activity: Happy to help. I will ask four short questions and then send your request to your manager for approval.

    - kind: Question
      id: q_type
      variable: init:Topic.LeaveType
      prompt: Which type of leave do you need? Type annual, sick, unpaid or special.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_leave_key
      variable: init:Topic.LeaveKey
      value: =Lower(Trim(Topic.LeaveType))

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_type
      conditions:
        - id: cond_type_invalid
          condition: =!(Topic.LeaveKey in ["annual", "sick", "unpaid", "special"])
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_type_invalid
              activity: I only know annual, sick, unpaid and special leave.
            - kind: Question
              id: q_type_again
              variable: Topic.LeaveType
              prompt: Which type of leave do you need?
              entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true
            - kind: SetVariable
              id: sv_leave_key_again
              variable: Topic.LeaveKey
              value: =Lower(Trim(Topic.LeaveType))

    - kind: Question
      id: q_start
      variable: init:Topic.StartDate
      prompt: What is the first day of your leave?
      entity: DateTimePrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: Question
      id: q_end
      variable: init:Topic.EndDate
      prompt: And the last day of your leave?
      entity: DateTimePrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_dates
      conditions:
        - id: cond_range_invalid
          condition: =Topic.EndDate < Topic.StartDate
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_invalid
              activity: The last day is before the first day. Please enter the last day again.
            - kind: Question
              id: q_end_again
              variable: Topic.EndDate
              prompt: What is the last day of your leave?
              entity: DateTimePrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_days
      variable: init:Topic.CalendarDays
      value: =DateDiff(Topic.StartDate, Topic.EndDate, TimeUnit.Days) + 1

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_start_text
      variable: init:Topic.StartText
      value: =Text(Topic.StartDate, "yyyy-mm-dd")

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_end_text
      variable: init:Topic.EndText
      value: =Text(Topic.EndDate, "yyyy-mm-dd")

    - kind: Question
      id: q_reason
      variable: init:Topic.Reason
      prompt: Add a short note for your manager, or type "none".
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_summary
      activity: |-
        Please check your request:
        Type: {Topic.LeaveKey}
        From: {Topic.StartText}
        To: {Topic.EndText}
        Calendar days: {Topic.CalendarDays}
        Note: {Topic.Reason}

    - kind: Question
      id: q_confirm
      variable: init:Topic.Confirmed
      prompt: Shall I submit this request?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_confirm
      conditions:
        - id: cond_yes
          condition: =Topic.Confirmed = true
          actions:
            - kind: InvokeFlowAction
              id: flow_submit
              input:
                binding:
                  text: =Topic.LeaveKey
                  text_1: =Topic.StartText
                  text_2: =Topic.EndText
                  text_3: =Topic.Reason
                  text_4: =User.Email
              output:
                binding:
                  requestid: Topic.RequestId
              flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_done
              activity: Your request {Topic.RequestId} was sent for approval. You will get an email as soon as your manager decides.

            - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
              id: log_submit
              eventName: LeaveRequestSubmitted
              properties: "={LeaveType: Topic.LeaveKey, Days: Topic.CalendarDays}"

      elseActions:
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_cancel
          activity: No problem, nothing was submitted. Say "request leave" to start again.

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main
      clearTopicQueue: true

=== How to use ===
1. Create a new topic from blank, open More (...) > Open code editor and replace the content with the YAML above.
2. Build the flow with the trigger 'Run a flow from Copilot' and five text inputs (type, start, end, note, email). Add an approval and an Outlook email, and return requestid with the 'Respond to the agent' action.
3. Save the topic once, then open the flow Action node in the authoring canvas and re-select your flow. Copilot Studio replaces the placeholder flowId and fixes the binding names for your flow.
4. Adjust the accepted leave types to your HR policy and add or remove trigger phrases. Keep five to ten phrases for classic orchestration.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Leaving the placeholder flowId in place: the topic saves but fails at runtime with a flow-not-found error.
- Using a Question node without init: for the first assignment of a variable. Use init:Topic.Name once, then plain Topic.Name for later writes.
- Counting working days with DateDiff alone. The topic counts calendar days; weekends and public holidays must be handled in the flow or in a holiday table.
- Forgetting that DateTimePrebuiltEntity can interpret vague input such as 'next Friday'. Always show the interpreted date back to the user, as the summary message does.
- Reusing identical node IDs when you copy the topic. IDs must be unique inside one topic.

=== Testing ===
- Use the test panel and enter an end date before the start date. The topic must ask for the end date a second time.
- Answer No at the confirmation and check that the flow run history shows no new run.
- Answer Yes and check the flow run, the approval created and the custom telemetry event LeaveRequestSubmitted in Application Insights if connected.

title: Copilot Studio topic: personalised onboarding checklist for new hires
summary: Topic YAML that builds a first-week checklist from role, start date and remote work using Power Fx Switch and If, with timing hints and telemetry. No flow needed.
body:
A self-contained onboarding topic. It asks for the area, the first working day and whether the person works remotely, then assembles the checklist text in Power Fx variables and sends it as one message. Because it needs no flow, it is a good first topic for an HR or IT welcome agent.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Builds a personal first-week checklist for a new employee based on role, start date, remote work and equipment needs.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: New hire checklist
    triggerQueries:
      - What do I need to do in my first week
      - Onboarding checklist
      - I am a new employee
      - I start next Monday what should I prepare
      - New joiner tasks

  actions:
    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_welcome
      activity: Welcome to the team. Let me build a checklist that fits your situation.

    - kind: Question
      id: q_role
      variable: init:Topic.Role
      prompt: Which area will you work in? Type office, engineering or sales.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_role_key
      variable: init:Topic.RoleKey
      value: =Lower(Trim(Topic.Role))

    - kind: Question
      id: q_start
      variable: init:Topic.StartDate
      prompt: What is your first working day?
      entity: DateTimePrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: Question
      id: q_remote
      variable: init:Topic.IsRemote
      prompt: Will you mostly work remotely?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_days_to_start
      variable: init:Topic.DaysToStart
      value: =DateDiff(Today(), Topic.StartDate, TimeUnit.Days)

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_start_text
      variable: init:Topic.StartText
      value: =Text(Topic.StartDate, "dddd, d mmmm yyyy")

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_role_tasks
      variable: init:Topic.RoleTasks
      value: =Switch(Topic.RoleKey, "engineering", "- Request admin rights through the privileged access form" & Char(10) & "- Join the engineering team in Microsoft Teams", "sales", "- Get access to the CRM and the sales playbook" & Char(10) & "- Shadow two customer calls", "- Meet your team lead for a walkthrough of the office tools")

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_remote_tasks
      variable: init:Topic.RemoteTasks
      value: =If(Topic.IsRemote, "- Test your home network and headset before day one" & Char(10) & "- Confirm the shipping address for your laptop", "- Pick up your badge at reception")

    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_checklist
      activity: |-
        Your checklist for {Topic.StartText}:
        - Sign the contract and send the bank details to HR
        - Set up multifactor authentication on your phone
        {Topic.RemoteTasks}
        {Topic.RoleTasks}
        - Complete the security awareness training in your first week

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_timing
      conditions:
        - id: cond_soon
          condition: =Topic.DaysToStart >= 0 && Topic.DaysToStart <= 3
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_soon
              activity: You start in {Topic.DaysToStart} days. Please finish the first two items before day one.
        - id: cond_past
          condition: =Topic.DaysToStart < 0
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_past
              activity: Your start date is already in the past. If you are missing access to anything, tell me what and I will point you to the right team.

    - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
      id: log_checklist
      eventName: OnboardingChecklistShown
      properties: "={Role: Topic.RoleKey, Remote: Topic.IsRemote}"

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Create a blank topic, open the code editor and paste the YAML.
2. Replace the generic tasks with your real onboarding steps. Keep every task on its own line by joining the lines with Char(10).
3. Add more roles by extending the prompt and the Switch expression. The last argument of Switch is the default branch.
4. Optionally add a second topic that reacts to the phrase 'tell me more' and links to your onboarding page in SharePoint.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Writing the newline as a backslash n inside the Power Fx string. Power Fx does not interpret it, so use Char(10).
- Switching to a multiple choice question and comparing its variable with a plain string. Choice values are not strings, so the condition can silently stay false. This sample uses validated text input; if you use the choice picker, test every condition in the test panel.
- Forgetting that DateTimePrebuiltEntity may return a date with a time part. DateDiff with TimeUnit.Days handles this, a direct subtraction does not.
- Making the checklist too long. More than eight items in one message are rarely read; split by week instead.

=== Testing ===
- Pick each role once and compare the message text with your expectation.
- Enter a start date three days from today and check that the reminder branch fires, then enter a date in the past.
- Switch the test panel to the track-between-topics view to confirm only this topic ran.

title: Copilot Studio topic: invoice approval status lookup with input validation
summary: Topic YAML that validates an invoice number with IsMatch, retries once, calls a lookup flow and answers differently for pending, approved, unknown and other states.
body:
Employees often ask where their invoice is in the approval chain. This topic validates the invoice number format locally, so that the flow is only called with clean input, then calls a lookup flow and branches on the returned status. The flow can read from Dataverse, a SharePoint list or an ERP API.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Looks up the approval status of an invoice by its number and tells the requester who has to approve next.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Invoice approval status
    triggerQueries:
      - Where is my invoice
      - Check invoice status
      - Is invoice approved
      - Status of my invoice approval
      - Who needs to approve my invoice

  actions:
    - kind: Question
      id: q_invoice
      variable: init:Topic.InvoiceNumber
      prompt: What is the invoice number? It looks like INV-123456.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_format
      conditions:
        - id: cond_bad_format
          condition: =!IsMatch(Topic.InvoiceNumber, "INV-\d{6}", MatchOptions.Complete)
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_bad_format
              activity: That does not look like an invoice number. The format is INV- followed by six digits.
            - kind: Question
              id: q_invoice_again
              variable: Topic.InvoiceNumber
              prompt: Please type the invoice number again.
              entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_format_retry
      conditions:
        - id: cond_still_bad
          condition: =!IsMatch(Topic.InvoiceNumber, "INV-\d{6}", MatchOptions.Complete)
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_give_up
              activity: I could not read the number. Please look it up in the invoice mailbox and try again later.
            - kind: EndDialog
              id: end_give_up
              clearTopicQueue: true

    - kind: InvokeFlowAction
      id: flow_lookup
      input:
        binding:
          text: =Upper(Topic.InvoiceNumber)
          text_1: =User.Email
      output:
        binding:
          status: Topic.Status
          approver: Topic.Approver
          amount: Topic.Amount
      flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_status
      conditions:
        - id: cond_notfound
          condition: =IsBlank(Topic.Status) || Topic.Status = "NotFound"
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_notfound
              activity: I found no invoice with that number that was submitted by you.
        - id: cond_pending
          condition: =Topic.Status = "Pending"
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_pending
              activity: Invoice {Topic.InvoiceNumber} for {Topic.Amount} is waiting for approval by {Topic.Approver}.
        - id: cond_approved
          condition: =Topic.Status = "Approved"
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_approved
              activity: Invoice {Topic.InvoiceNumber} was approved by {Topic.Approver}. Payment follows the normal run on Thursday.
      elseActions:
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_other
          activity: Invoice {Topic.InvoiceNumber} has the status {Topic.Status}. Please contact accounts payable for details.

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Build a flow with the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger (inputs: invoice number, requester email) that looks up the invoice and returns status, approver and amount as text outputs.
2. Paste the YAML, save, then re-select your flow in the flow Action node so that the real flowId and output names are written.
3. Change the regular expression in IsMatch to your own number scheme and adjust the Thursday payment sentence or remove it.
4. Make the flow filter by requester email, so that people can only see their own invoices.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Putting anchors ^ and $ into the pattern and also using MatchOptions.Complete. Complete already forces a full match, so use one of them.
- Returning a number as a real number in the flow and then concatenating it in a message. Return text to avoid locale formatting surprises.
- Validating only the first answer. The second input is checked again in cg_format_retry; without that second check an invalid retry would reach the flow.
- Not handling the empty result. The IsBlank check protects against a flow that returns nothing when the row is missing.
- Exposing invoices of other people. Always pass the requester and filter in the flow, never only in the topic.

=== Testing ===
- Enter abc, then abc again and verify the dialog ends politely after the second failure. Then enter abc followed by a valid number such as INV-123456 and verify that the lookup runs.
- Test one invoice for every status your flow can return, including a number that does not exist.
- Open the flow run history and confirm the uppercase invoice number and the requester email arrived.

title: Copilot Studio topic: IT helpdesk ticket with priority rules and escalation
summary: Topic YAML that gathers category, impact and description, derives a priority with Power Fx, confirms, calls a ticket flow and escalates critical cases to a second topic.
body:
A typical first-line support topic. Instead of asking the user to rate urgency, it asks how many people are blocked and derives the priority in Power Fx. This produces more consistent tickets. The flow behind it can write to Dataverse, ServiceNow or a SharePoint list; the topic only needs the ticket number back.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Creates an IT helpdesk ticket after collecting category, urgency and a description, and escalates critical issues.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Create IT ticket
    triggerQueries:
      - Open a ticket
      - I have a problem with my laptop
      - Report an IT issue
      - Something is broken
      - Create a helpdesk request

  actions:
    - kind: Question
      id: q_category
      variable: init:Topic.Category
      prompt: What is the issue about? Type hardware, software, account or network.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_category_key
      variable: init:Topic.CategoryKey
      value: =If(Lower(Trim(Topic.Category)) in ["hardware", "software", "account", "network"], Lower(Trim(Topic.Category)), "other")

    - kind: Question
      id: q_urgency
      variable: init:Topic.Urgency
      prompt: How many people are blocked? Type a number, or 0 if you can still work.
      entity: NumberPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_priority
      variable: init:Topic.Priority
      value: =If(Topic.Urgency >= 10, "Critical", If(Topic.Urgency >= 1, "High", "Normal"))

    - kind: Question
      id: q_description
      variable: init:Topic.Description
      prompt: Describe the problem in one or two sentences. Include error messages if you have them.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_short
      conditions:
        - id: cond_too_short
          condition: =Len(Trim(Topic.Description)) < 15
          actions:
            - kind: Question
              id: q_description_more
              variable: Topic.Description
              prompt: Please add a few more details so the technician can start right away.
              entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_review
      activity: |-
        I will create this ticket:
        Category: {Topic.CategoryKey}
        Priority: {Topic.Priority}
        Description: {Topic.Description}

    - kind: Question
      id: q_confirm
      variable: init:Topic.Confirmed
      prompt: Is that correct?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_confirmed
      conditions:
        - id: cond_confirmed
          condition: =Topic.Confirmed = true
          actions:
            - kind: InvokeFlowAction
              id: flow_ticket
              input:
                binding:
                  text: =Topic.CategoryKey
                  text_1: =Topic.Priority
                  text_2: =Topic.Description
                  text_3: =User.Email
                  text_4: =System.Conversation.Id
              output:
                binding:
                  ticketnumber: Topic.TicketNumber
              flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_created
              activity: Ticket {Topic.TicketNumber} was created. You will receive updates by email.

            - kind: ConditionGroup
              id: cg_critical
              conditions:
                - id: cond_critical
                  condition: =Topic.Priority = "Critical"
                  actions:
                    - kind: SendActivity
                      id: msg_critical
                      activity: Because many people are blocked, I am also alerting the on-call technician.
                    # Replace the prefix with the schema name of your agent
                    - kind: BeginDialog
                      id: begin_escalate
                      dialog: contoso_helpdesk.topic.Escalate
      elseActions:
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_not_created
          activity: I did not create a ticket. You can start again at any time.

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Create the ticket flow with the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger, five text inputs and an output named ticketnumber.
2. Paste the YAML, save, open the flow Action node and select your flow so that Copilot Studio writes the real flowId.
3. Replace contoso_helpdesk in the BeginDialog node with the schema name of your own agent (shown in the agent details). Remove the node if you have no escalation topic.
4. Tune the thresholds in the Priority expression to your support model, for example 3 people for High.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Mixing up Topic.Urgency (a number) with the text priority. Keep them as two variables.
- Passing System.Conversation.Id to the flow but never storing it. Save it in the ticket so support can find the transcript.
- Asking for the description before the category. Users then write long free text and the category question feels redundant.
- Hard-coding the on-call phone number in the message. Read it from an environment variable or from the flow response.

=== Testing ===
- Test with 0, 3 and 12 blocked people and verify Normal, High and Critical in the summary.
- Enter a very short description and confirm the topic asks for more details once.
- Check that the ticket row contains the user email, priority and conversation ID.

title: Copilot Studio topic: SharePoint permission report request with admin check
summary: Topic YAML that checks the requester against an allow list, validates the site address, asks for the report type and starts a flow that emails the permission report.
body:
Governance teams get many requests of the form 'who can see this site'. This topic gives authorised people a chat entry point for that request. The topic itself only validates and routes; the report is built by a flow that calls the SharePoint REST API and emails the result. Authorisation is checked twice: in the topic for a friendly message, and again in the flow, which must never trust the topic alone.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Lets an authorised site owner or administrator request a SharePoint permission report for one site, delivered by email.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: SharePoint permission report
    triggerQueries:
      - Who has access to my SharePoint site
      - Send me a permission report
      - Audit site permissions
      - Show unique permissions for a site
      - External sharing report

  actions:
    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_requester
      variable: init:Topic.RequesterEmail
      value: =Lower(User.Email)

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_authorised
      conditions:
        - id: cond_not_allowed
          condition: =!(Topic.RequesterEmail in ["admin1@contoso.example", "admin2@contoso.example", "compliance@contoso.example"])
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_denied
              activity: Permission reports are limited to the SharePoint administrators. Please open a ticket if you need one.
            - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
              id: log_denied
              eventName: PermissionReportDenied
              properties: "={Requester: Topic.RequesterEmail}"
            - kind: EndDialog
              id: end_denied
              clearTopicQueue: true

    - kind: Question
      id: q_site
      variable: init:Topic.SiteUrl
      prompt: Paste the address of the site, for example https://contoso.sharepoint.example/sites/Finance
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_site_clean
      variable: init:Topic.SiteClean
      value: =Substitute(Trim(Topic.SiteUrl), "/SitePages/Home.aspx", "")

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_site
      conditions:
        - id: cond_site_invalid
          condition: =!StartsWith(Lower(Topic.SiteClean), "https://contoso.sharepoint.example/sites/")
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_site_invalid
              activity: The address must start with https://contoso.sharepoint.example/sites/. Please start again and paste the full site address.
            - kind: EndDialog
              id: end_site_invalid
              clearTopicQueue: true

    - kind: Question
      id: q_scope
      variable: init:Topic.ReportScope
      prompt: Which report do you need? Type unique for lists with unique permissions, or external for sharing with guests.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_scope_key
      variable: init:Topic.ScopeKey
      value: =If(StartsWith(Lower(Trim(Topic.ReportScope)), "ext"), "external", "unique")

    - kind: InvokeFlowAction
      id: flow_report
      input:
        binding:
          text: =Topic.SiteClean
          text_1: =Topic.ScopeKey
          text_2: =Topic.RequesterEmail
      output:
        binding:
          itemcount: Topic.ItemCount
      flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_done
      activity: The report for {Topic.SiteClean} is ready. It found {Topic.ItemCount} entries and was sent to {Topic.RequesterEmail}.

    - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
      id: log_done
      eventName: PermissionReportRequested
      properties: "={Site: Topic.SiteClean, Scope: Topic.ScopeKey, Requester: Topic.RequesterEmail}"

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Replace the three sample addresses with your administrators, or better, read the allow list from a Dataverse table in the flow and return an 'allowed' output.
2. Replace contoso.sharepoint.example with your tenant host name in both the condition and the message.
3. Build the report flow with the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger (site, scope, requester) and return the number of rows as itemcount.
4. Publish the agent only to the channel where administrators work, for example a Teams app limited to a security group.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Relying on the topic for security. A user who can call the flow in another way bypasses the check; validate the requester in the flow too.
- Comparing the email without Lower(). Entra ID can return the address in mixed case.
- Accepting any URL. Without the StartsWith check, the flow would try to read arbitrary sites and fail with unclear errors.
- Returning the full report into the chat. Large permission lists belong in an email or a file, not in a message.

=== Testing ===
- Test with an address that is not on the allow list and confirm the report flow is never started.
- Paste a site address with a trailing /SitePages/Home.aspx and check that it is cleaned.
- Open the flow run and confirm site, scope and requester arrived as expected.

title: Copilot Studio topic: announcement drafting and posting to Teams channels
summary: Topic YAML that collects audience and text, enforces a length limit with Power Fx, shows a preview and posts to the matching Teams channel via a flow after confirmation.
body:
Internal communication teams often want a controlled way to publish short notices. This topic maps a simple audience keyword to a channel inside the flow, enforces a length limit, shows a preview and only posts after the user confirms. The channel IDs stay in the flow, so the topic never contains tenant-specific identifiers.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Helps a user draft a short announcement and posts it to the right Microsoft Teams channel through a flow after confirmation.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Post a team announcement
    triggerQueries:
      - Post an announcement
      - Tell the team about the maintenance window
      - Send a message to the channel
      - Publish a notice in Teams
      - I want to announce something

  actions:
    - kind: Question
      id: q_audience
      variable: init:Topic.Audience
      prompt: Who should see it? Type all-staff, it or sales.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_audience_key
      variable: init:Topic.AudienceKey
      value: =Switch(Lower(Trim(Topic.Audience)), "it", "it", "sales", "sales", "all-staff")

    - kind: Question
      id: q_text
      variable: init:Topic.MessageText
      prompt: What is the message? Keep it under 400 characters.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_length
      conditions:
        - id: cond_too_long
          condition: =Len(Topic.MessageText) > 400
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_too_long
              activity: Your message is longer than 400 characters. Teams announcements work best when short, so please shorten it.
            - kind: Question
              id: q_text_again
              variable: Topic.MessageText
              prompt: Please enter a shorter version.
              entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: Question
      id: q_important
      variable: init:Topic.IsImportant
      prompt: Is this important enough to mark it as an urgent announcement?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_subject
      variable: init:Topic.Subject
      value: =If(Topic.IsImportant, "Urgent announcement", "Announcement")

    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_preview
      activity: |-
        Preview for the {Topic.AudienceKey} channel:
        {Topic.Subject}
        {Topic.MessageText}

    - kind: Question
      id: q_confirm
      variable: init:Topic.Confirmed
      prompt: Shall I post it now?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_post
      conditions:
        - id: cond_post
          condition: =Topic.Confirmed = true
          actions:
            - kind: InvokeFlowAction
              id: flow_post
              input:
                binding:
                  text: =Topic.AudienceKey
                  text_1: =Topic.Subject
                  text_2: =Topic.MessageText
                  text_3: =User.DisplayName
              output:
                binding:
                  posted: Topic.Posted
              flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_posted
              activity: Done. Your announcement is live in the channel.
      elseActions:
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_discarded
          activity: I discarded the draft.

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Build a flow with the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger and four text inputs (audience, subject, text, author). Use a Switch on the audience to select the Teams team and channel for 'Post message in a chat or channel'.
2. Paste the YAML, save and re-select the flow in the flow Action node.
3. Add the allowed audiences to the question prompt and to the Switch expression. The last Switch argument is the default.
4. Limit who can use the agent with the sharing settings or a security group, because the flow posts under the flow owner's or Flow bot identity.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Letting every user post to all-staff. Combine the topic with an allow list like the permission report topic.
- Skipping the preview. People paste half-finished text, and a posted message in a large channel cannot be recalled cleanly.
- Putting channel IDs into the topic. They belong in the flow or in an environment variable per environment.
- Interpolating Power Fx directly into a message and getting an empty value. If a value is blank, calculate it in a SetVariable node first.

=== Testing ===
- Enter a message longer than 400 characters and confirm the shortening loop.
- Answer No at the confirmation and verify nothing was posted.
- Post to each audience once in a test team and check the subject line and author in the channel message.

title: Copilot Studio topic: expense policy checker using Power Fx rules
summary: Topic YAML that answers limit, approver and receipt questions for an expense with nested Power Fx If and Switch expressions, without any flow or connector.
body:
Policy questions are the perfect use case for deterministic logic: the answer must be the same every time. This topic encodes limits, approval tiers and receipt rules in Power Fx so no model has to guess. Keep the numbers in SetVariable nodes at the top, or load them from a Dataverse table in a flow, so that finance can change them without editing the dialog logic.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Tells an employee whether an expense is within policy, who has to approve it and which receipt rules apply.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Expense policy check
    triggerQueries:
      - Can I expense this
      - Expense limit for dinner
      - Who approves my travel costs
      - Do I need a receipt
      - Is this expense allowed

  actions:
    - kind: Question
      id: q_type
      variable: init:Topic.ExpenseType
      prompt: What kind of expense is it? Type meal, travel, hotel or equipment.
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_type_key
      variable: init:Topic.TypeKey
      value: =Lower(Trim(Topic.ExpenseType))

    - kind: Question
      id: q_amount
      variable: init:Topic.Amount
      prompt: What is the amount in euros?
      entity: NumberPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: false

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_limit
      variable: init:Topic.Limit
      value: =Switch(Topic.TypeKey, "meal", 40, "travel", 500, "hotel", 180, "equipment", 1000, 0)

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_approver
      variable: init:Topic.Approver
      value: =If(Topic.Amount <= 100, "your team lead", If(Topic.Amount <= 1000, "your department head", "the finance director"))

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_receipt
      variable: init:Topic.ReceiptRule
      value: =If(Topic.Amount > 25, "A receipt is required.", "No receipt is required below 25 euros.")

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_policy
      conditions:
        - id: cond_unknown
          condition: =Topic.Limit = 0
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_unknown
              activity: I do not know that expense type. Please choose meal, travel, hotel or equipment, or ask finance.
        - id: cond_within
          condition: =Topic.Amount <= Topic.Limit
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_within
              activity: This is within the limit of {Topic.Limit} euros for {Topic.TypeKey}. It needs approval from {Topic.Approver}. {Topic.ReceiptRule}
      elseActions:
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_over
          activity: This exceeds the limit of {Topic.Limit} euros for {Topic.TypeKey}. You need an exception approved by the finance director before you submit it. {Topic.ReceiptRule}

    - kind: Question
      id: q_more
      variable: init:Topic.AnotherOne
      prompt: Do you want to check another expense?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_more
      conditions:
        - id: cond_again
          condition: =Topic.AnotherOne = true
          actions:
            # Replace the prefix with the schema name of your agent
            - kind: BeginDialog
              id: begin_self
              dialog: contoso_hr.topic.ExpensePolicyCheck

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Create a topic named ExpensePolicyCheck, open the code editor and paste the YAML. The name must match the last part of the BeginDialog reference.
2. Replace contoso_hr with the schema name of your agent, or delete the last ConditionGroup if you do not want the loop.
3. Edit limits and tiers in the Switch and If expressions to match your travel policy and currency.
4. If the limits change often, move them to a table and read them through a flow.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Using different units in the question and in the limits, for example net versus gross amounts. State clearly which one you expect.
- Forgetting the default argument of Switch. Without it, an unknown type returns blank and the comparison fails.
- Letting the topic loop back to itself without resetting variables. With alwaysPrompt set to false a question is skipped when its variable already holds a value, so the next round may reuse old answers; set alwaysPrompt to true for questions that must be asked again, or reset the variables first.
- Presenting the result as a decision. The topic gives guidance; approval still happens in the real expense system.

=== Testing ===
- Test each type once below, at and above its limit.
- Test 25, 26 and 1001 euros to verify the receipt and approver boundaries.
- Type a nonsense category and verify the fallback message.

title: Copilot Studio topic: grounded HR policy answers with feedback and logging
summary: Topic YAML using CreateSearchQuery and SearchAndSummarizeContent for generative answers with custom instructions, a disclaimer, thumbs-style feedback and telemetry for gaps.
body:
When an HR agent answers from SharePoint pages, you want control over tone, sources and fallbacks. This topic runs the generative answers node explicitly, so you can add instructions, a disclaimer and a feedback question, and log unanswered questions. The unanswered log becomes the backlog for improving the handbook.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Answers HR policy questions with generative answers grounded in the agent's knowledge sources and offers a human contact when no answer is found.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: HR policy question
    triggerQueries:
      - What is the home office policy
      - How many vacation days do I have
      - Parental leave rules
      - Policy for working abroad
      - What does the handbook say about

  actions:
    - kind: CreateSearchQuery
      id: create_query
      userInput: =System.Activity.Text
      result: Topic.SearchQuery

    - kind: SearchAndSummarizeContent
      id: search_policy
      variable: Topic.Answer
      userInput: =Topic.SearchQuery.SearchQuery
      additionalInstructions: Answer only from the HR handbook and policy pages. Quote the policy name and the valid-from date if available. If the sources conflict, say so and name both. Never give legal advice.

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_answer
      conditions:
        - id: cond_answered
          condition: =!IsBlank(Topic.Answer)
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_disclaimer
              activity: Please note that the HR handbook on the intranet is the binding source if anything differs.

            - kind: Question
              id: q_helpful
              variable: init:Topic.Helpful
              prompt: Did this answer your question?
              entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

            - kind: ConditionGroup
              id: cg_helpful
              conditions:
                - id: cond_not_helpful
                  condition: =Topic.Helpful = false
                  actions:
                    - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
                      id: log_not_helpful
                      eventName: HrAnswerNotHelpful
                      properties: "={Question: System.Activity.Text, Conversation: System.Conversation.Id}"
                    - kind: SendActivity
                      id: msg_contact_after
                      activity: Sorry about that. Please write to the HR service desk and mention conversation {System.Conversation.Id}.

      elseActions:
        - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
          id: log_no_answer
          eventName: HrNoAnswer
          properties: "={Question: System.Activity.Text}"
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_no_answer
          activity: I could not find that in the HR handbook. Please contact the HR service desk, and I will pass this question on to improve the handbook.

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Add your HR SharePoint sites or the handbook PDF as knowledge sources of the agent first. The node searches the agent's knowledge sources.
2. Paste the YAML into a new topic. If you use generative orchestration, the topic description in modelDescription helps the orchestrator route policy questions here.
3. Adapt additionalInstructions to your rules, for example language, tone, mandatory citations and topics the agent must not answer.
4. Connect Application Insights to the agent and build a simple query on the events HrNoAnswer and HrAnswerNotHelpful.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Expecting the node to find content that the user may not read. Knowledge from SharePoint honours the signed-in user's permissions, so test with a normal account, not an admin.
- Writing long instructions that contradict each other. Keep three or four clear rules.
- Using the topic as the only fallback. Conversations that never match any trigger phrase need an OnUnknownIntent topic with the same search steps.
- Treating the answer as legal advice. Keep the disclaimer and the pointer to the binding source.

=== Testing ===
- Ask a question that the handbook answers and check that the policy name appears.
- Ask something that is not covered and confirm that the no-answer branch logs the event.
- Answer No to the feedback question and check the telemetry event and the message.

title: Copilot Studio topic: customer satisfaction rating with low-score follow-up
summary: Topic YAML that collects a 1 to 5 rating, validates the range, asks for a comment only for low scores, stores the result with a flow and logs a telemetry event.
body:
A short satisfaction survey that you can trigger by phrase or call from other topics at the end of a conversation. It avoids survey fatigue: only dissatisfied users get a second question. The score and comment are stored by a flow in Dataverse or a SharePoint list, and an additional telemetry event feeds Application Insights dashboards.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of a new topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
modelDescription: Asks the user to rate the conversation from 1 to 5, collects a comment for low scores and stores the result through a flow.
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRecognizedIntent
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Rate this conversation
    triggerQueries:
      - Give feedback
      - Rate this chat
      - I want to leave a rating
      - Feedback about the assistant
      - How did you do

  actions:
    - kind: Question
      id: q_score
      variable: init:Topic.Score
      prompt: How helpful was this conversation? Please give a number from 1 (not helpful) to 5 (very helpful).
      entity: NumberPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true
      unrecognizedPrompt: Please answer with a number from 1 to 5.

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_range
      conditions:
        - id: cond_out_of_range
          condition: =Topic.Score < 1 || Topic.Score > 5
          actions:
            - kind: Question
              id: q_score_again
              variable: Topic.Score
              prompt: The score must be between 1 and 5. What is your rating?
              entity: NumberPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_clamp
      variable: Topic.Score
      value: =Max(1, Min(5, Topic.Score))

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_comment_default
      variable: init:Topic.Comment
      value: =""

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_low
      conditions:
        - id: cond_low
          condition: =Topic.Score <= 3
          actions:
            - kind: Question
              id: q_comment
              variable: Topic.Comment
              prompt: I am sorry I fell short. What should I have done better?
              entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_sentiment
      variable: init:Topic.Bucket
      value: =If(Topic.Score >= 4, "positive", If(Topic.Score = 3, "neutral", "negative"))

    - kind: InvokeFlowAction
      id: flow_store
      input:
        binding:
          number: =Topic.Score
          text: =Topic.Comment
          text_1: =System.Conversation.Id
          text_2: =Topic.Bucket
      output:
        binding:
          saved: Topic.Saved
      flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

    - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
      id: log_csat
      eventName: ConversationRated
      properties: "={Score: Topic.Score, Bucket: Topic.Bucket}"

    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_thanks
      activity: Thank you for your feedback. It helps us improve this assistant.

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Create a flow with the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger (number score, three text inputs) that creates a row in a feedback table and returns saved as text.
2. Paste the YAML and select the flow in the flow Action node.
3. Call the topic at the end of your main topics with a Redirect or BeginDialog node, or let it be triggered by the phrases.
4. Build a Power BI or Application Insights view on Score and Bucket.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Storing an empty comment as null in Dataverse. The topic sets an empty string first, so that the flow input is never missing.
- Asking for feedback after every single answer. Ask once per conversation.
- Forgetting that NumberPrebuiltEntity also accepts text such as 'four'. Keep the range check anyway; the sv_clamp node forces the score into 1 to 5 even if the second answer is out of range as well.
- Storing user email together with the comment without a privacy review. This sample stores only the conversation ID.

=== Testing ===
- Enter 0 and 9 and check that the topic asks again.
- Enter 2 and 5 and verify the comment question appears only for 2.
- Check the stored row and the telemetry event for each test.

title: Copilot Studio escalation topic that collects context and files a callback case
summary: Escalate system topic in YAML that gathers a summary and callback number, detects after-hours with Power Fx, calls a case flow and sets realistic expectations.
body:
Every agent needs a clean exit to a human. This version of the Escalate topic does not hand over silently: it collects a one-line summary and an optional phone number, passes the conversation ID so that support can read the transcript, and tells the user honestly when the team is offline. Without a live-agent channel configured, this asynchronous handoff is the pragmatic option.

=== YAML (paste into the code editor of the Escalate system topic) ===
kind: AdaptiveDialog
beginDialog:
  kind: OnEscalate
  id: main
  intent:
    displayName: Escalate
    includeInOnSelectIntent: false
    triggerQueries:
      - Talk to a person
      - I need a human
      - Speak to an agent
      - Connect me to support
      - This is not helping

  actions:
    - kind: SendActivity
      id: msg_intro
      activity: I will pass this to a colleague. A few details will save you from repeating yourself.

    - kind: Question
      id: q_summary
      variable: init:Topic.Summary
      prompt: In one sentence, what do you need help with?
      entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: Question
      id: q_callback
      variable: init:Topic.WantsCallback
      prompt: Should a colleague call you back instead of writing an email?
      entity: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
      alwaysPrompt: true

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_phone
      conditions:
        - id: cond_callback
          condition: =Topic.WantsCallback = true
          actions:
            - kind: Question
              id: q_phone
              variable: init:Topic.Phone
              prompt: Which phone number should we call?
              entity: StringPrebuiltEntity
              alwaysPrompt: true
      elseActions:
        - kind: SetVariable
          id: sv_phone_none
          variable: init:Topic.Phone
          value: ="none"

    - kind: SetVariable
      id: sv_after_hours
      variable: init:Topic.AfterHours
      value: =Hour(Now()) < 8 || Hour(Now()) >= 18 || Weekday(Now(), StartOfWeek.Monday) > 5

    - kind: InvokeFlowAction
      id: flow_handoff
      input:
        binding:
          text: =Topic.Summary
          text_1: =User.Email
          text_2: =Topic.Phone
          text_3: =System.Conversation.Id
          text_4: =Text(Topic.AfterHours)
      output:
        binding:
          caseid: Topic.CaseId
      flowId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

    - kind: ConditionGroup
      id: cg_hours
      conditions:
        - id: cond_after_hours
          condition: =Topic.AfterHours = true
          actions:
            - kind: SendActivity
              id: msg_after_hours
              activity: Our team is offline right now. Your request {Topic.CaseId} will be handled on the next working day before noon.
      elseActions:
        - kind: SendActivity
          id: msg_hours
          activity: Your request {Topic.CaseId} is with the support team. You will hear from us within two hours.

    - kind: LogCustomTelemetryEvent
      id: log_escalation
      eventName: EscalationRequested
      properties: "={Case: Topic.CaseId, Callback: Topic.WantsCallback}"

    - kind: EndDialog
      id: end_main

=== How to use ===
1. Open the existing Escalate system topic under System topics, open the code editor and replace its content. Keep a copy of the original.
2. Create the case flow with the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger and five text inputs. Create a Dataverse row or ticket, notify a Teams channel and return caseid.
3. Adjust the opening hours in the AfterHours expression. Hour and Weekday use the time zone of the user's locale, so check this for global teams.
4. If you use a live-agent integration, add its transfer node after the flow call and keep the callback branch as the fallback.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Replacing the system topic and forgetting includeInOnSelectIntent: false, which makes the topic show up in disambiguation lists.
- Promising an answer time that the team cannot meet. The two-hour promise must match your real service level.
- Collecting too many details. Three questions are the maximum before users abandon the handoff.
- Ignoring time zones. Now() reflects the conversation locale; use the flow to convert if your users are spread across regions.

=== Testing ===
- Type 'talk to a person' and check that this topic is triggered instead of a normal answer.
- Test once with a callback and once without; the flow must receive the string none for the phone.
- Change the opening hours temporarily to test both the after-hours and the in-hours message.
